title: Acceptance Criteria and Example-Based Specifications
learningObjectives: Explain the purpose and value of Acceptance Criteria and Example-Based Specifications.
Apply acceptance criteria and example-based specifications to a Python project scenario.
Identify decisions and trade-offs relevant to acceptance criteria and example-based specifications.
Review common mistakes and risks in acceptance criteria and example-based specifications.
Produce a verifiable project artifact using acceptance criteria and example-based specifications principles.

understand.concept: Acceptance criteria define observable conditions that demonstrate a requirement has been met. They should be specific and testable. Example-based specifications describe inputs, actions and expected outcomes, including boundary and failure cases.
understand.whyItMatters: Testable criteria connect user expectations to implementation and verification.
understand.analogy: A delivery checklist defines what must be present and what counts as damage.
understand.analogyLimit: Examples cannot cover every possible input; risk analysis and more tests remain necessary.
understand.summary: Acceptance Criteria and Example-Based Specifications helps learners plan and deliver maintainable Python projects.

explain.narrative: Write checkable conditions for each requirement. Given/When/Then describes starting context, action and observable result. Include normal behaviour, invalid input, boundaries and permissions. Avoid vague criteria such as works well.

examples.title: Acceptance scenario
examples.code:
case = {'given': 'saved learner', 'when': 'valid marks submitted', 'then': 'report updated'}
print(case['then'])
examples.explanation: A scenario defines context, action and outcome.

examples.title: Boundary
examples.code:
def valid_mark(x): return 0 <= x <= 100
print(valid_mark(100), valid_mark(101))

examples.title: Required field
examples.explanation: Whitespace-only input is not a valid name.

practise.guidedTask: Write criteria for adding a student record, including valid, missing-name, invalid-mark and duplicate-ID cases.
practise.independentTask: Convert vague feature descriptions into Given/When/Then scenarios.
hints: Describe observable results rather than internal code.
Keep each criterion focused on one behaviour.
Specify exact expected messages where useful.
practise.challenge: Create an acceptance specification for a secure password-reset workflow.
validationCriteria: The project concept is accurately explained and applied.
All examples execute with documented output on Python 3.13.
The proposed artifact is testable and appropriate to stated requirements.
Trade-offs, limitations and relevant risks are acknowledged.
